newsitem.title: USA: US high-yield fund inflows $1.34 bln in latest wk.
newsitem.headline: US high-yield fund inflows $1.34 bln in latest wk.

text.p: Net cash inflows to U.S. corporate high-yield mutual funds totaled $1.34 billion in the week ended May 7, according to AMG Data Services.
This far surpassed the $760.1 million inflows recorded in the prior week, which were confirmed as the largest since AMG began tracking the data in 1992.

Inflows for the past four weeks more than offset the $1.58 billion of net cash outflows seen during the high-yield market downturn of March to mid-April. Volatility in flows have largely been attributed to "market timers," a specialized type of money manager known for making large, short-term investment based on price momentum.
Th figures represent cash flows to and from high-yield mutual funds that report on a weekly basis.
AMG, based in Arcata, Calif., is a U.S. mutual fund information company.
